papers.title: A High-Fidelity Cardiac Digital Twin for Assessing Rate-Dependent Responses: A Comparative Multi-scale Study of TT2 and Tomek Models in Stratified 3D Ventricles
papers.abstract: Cardiac digital twins (CDTs) provide a computational platform for personalized cardiac modeling, but their predictive behavior depends strongly on the selected ionic model and the representation of transmural electrophysiological heterogeneity. In this study, we developed a multiscale CDT validation framework that integrates physiologically optimized hierarchical configurations. Using single-cell (0D) models and three-dimensional (3D) patient-specific ventricular models, we implemented the ten Tusscher-Panfilov model (TT2) and Tomek ionic model and compared their electrophysiological responses across a range of pacing frequencies, with basic cycle lengths (BCLs) from 600 to 4000 ms. The results show that tissue-level electrical coupling substantially reshapes the intrinsic dynamical properties observed at the single-cell level. By benchmarking model outputs against clinical data, this study quantifies fidelity differences between the two ionic models across multiple scales and provides a scientific basis for ionic model selection and CDT construction.

papers.title: A novel model-based equation for size dependent mean recovery coefficients for spheres and other shapes
papers.abstract: Background: In NM-imaging, theoretical curves for the recovery coefficient (RC) of the signal maximum and mean are known for spheres and cubes, if a 3D Gaussian PSF is assumed. The RC of the maximum is also known for cylinders. For these and other shapes empirical equations with one or two fit-parameters have been utilized. Methods: An equation for the RC for large objects of arbitrary shape is derived and generalized into an empirical equation for smaller objects, which is verified by numerical simulations. The proposed equation is compared to published results on SPECT kidney phantom measurements and to PET measurements on the NEMA IEC PET body phantom with six spheres. Results: The signal loss (1-RC) for large spheres is inversely proportional to the radius, where the slope is proportional to the FWHM of the spatial resolution. For non-spherical shapes the generalized instead of the volume equivalent radius should be utilized. For smaller objects, an equation with one added empirical fit-parameter is presented. It is demonstrated that the EANM-guidelines' two-parameter logistic function results in a poor fit if the theoretical slope and inverse proportionality are forced and it gives a suboptimal fit when both parameters are fitted. Conclusions: A novel model-based equation for the mean RC-curve is derived. It can be used for arbitrary shapes as long as the sphericity is taken into account and it is accurate down to RC=10%. One parameter is directly related to the spatial resolution, while the other is a shape depending fit-parameter.

papers.title: EQUIP-RPT: A framework for objective evaluation of quantitative imaging methods in radiopharmaceutical therapies
papers.abstract: Quantitative imaging (QI) provides a non-invasive approach for dosimetry and quantitative response assessment in radiopharmaceutical therapies (RPTs). QI methods are being developed for instrumentation, acquisition, reconstruction, and image analysis. However, a key barrier to routine adoption of these methods is that evidence demonstrating reliable performance of QI methods on clinically relevant quantification tasks in RPTs remains limited. Our goal is to outline the Evaluation of Quantitative Imaging Performance in Radiopharmaceutical Therapy (EQUIP-RPT) framework, a structured approach for objective, task-based evaluation of QI methods for RPTs. We outline the EQUIP-RPT framework based on image-science and task-based image-quality evaluation methodology, practical considerations, and recent literature. The framework is organized around four linked design steps: (i) specification of the quantification task, (ii) design of the study population and imaging protocol, (iii) task-specific information extraction, and (iv) selection of figures of merit (FoMs). The EQUIP-RPT framework is presented in the context of four quantification tasks in RPT: activity uptake, absorbed dose, volumetric tumor burden, and lesion-level longitudinal quantifications. The framework distinguishes two paradigms for task-specific information extraction and organizes FoMs according to the performance attributes they characterize. We describe key elements to apply the EQUIP-RPT framework in simulation, physical phantom, and clinical studies. Finally, we show how EQUIP-RPT can be used to generate a quantitative claim based on the evaluation study. The EQUIP-RPT framework is designed to provide a structured approach for objective task-based evaluation of QI methods in RPTs, thereby facilitating clinical translation of these methods.

papers.title: Subwavelength registration of skull-compensating acoustic holograms via nonlinear parametric array feedback
papers.abstract: Realizing the potential of optimized acoustic holograms for applications like transcranial ultrasound requires sub-wavelength alignment accuracy (less than 1.5 mm at 1 MHz), which is difficult to achieve with current non-MRI optical neuro-navigation methods. To address the critical challenge of alignment, we leverage the parametric array (PA) signal as an alignment surrogate, a highly penetrative, low-frequency difference wave generated by the nonlinear mixing of two primary high-frequency beams. Simulations show that a misaligned skull-compensating lens increases the primary acoustic energy within the skull bone (volumetric energy trapping), which strengthens the nonlinear source of the PA signal. We also tested whether shear-mode conversion in bone contributes: 2D elastic simulations showed only a small (3-5%) increase in shear-type motion with misalignment, and the transmitted ex vivo bursts did not lengthen as a shear path would require. Pseudo-sound and microbubble artifacts were examined and found unlikely to explain the signal, consistent with the PA signal arising from the intrinsic nonlinearity of the bone. Minimizing this PA signal yields a noninvasive real-time feedback mechanism that achieves sub-wavelength alignment accuracy, outperforming standard neuronavigation. Our findings present a robust framework that supports the design of simple, economical, and high-performance transcranial ultrasound systems for high-precision neuro-interventions.

papers.title: A Low-Cost MR-Compatible Pneumatic Motion Phantom for Magnetic Resonance Imaging
papers.abstract: We describe the detailed design, construction, and testing of a simple, low-cost, open-source, exclusively pneumatic phantom for gated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies of cyclic motion. The overall phantom cost is approximately $200. It is designed to use widely-available materials and an easy-to-program, adaptable micro-controller. Image contrast is generated with air pumped through mineral oil. We demonstrate the utility of the phantom for simulating simple organ motion when developing and investigating image acquisition and reconstruction methods. Phantom motion was independently characterized by video analysis and found to be highly repeatable, with a cycle-to-cycle period variation of 0.6% and a stroke volume variation of 2.3%. The phantom does not generate electromagnetic interference, making it a suitable option for unshielded ultra-low field (ULF) MRI systems. To our knowledge, this work reports the first motion phantom to be imaged on an ULF MRI system

papers.title: Multi-UTE Myelin Fraction Mapping: Repeatability and Cross-Field-Strength Reproducibility at 1.5T and 3T
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the repeatability and cross-field-strength reproducibility (1.5T vs 3T) of in vivo cerebral myelin fraction (MF) mapping with multi-contrast dual-resolution 3D UTE (multi-UTE), and to compare it with magnetization transfer (MT)-based methods. Methods: MT methods provide an indirect myelin-sensitive measure derived from magnetization exchange between macromolecular and free-water proton pools, whereas multi-UTE targets the ultrashort-T2* signal components. In five healthy volunteers, multi-UTE and MT-based measurements were performed at 1.5T and 3T, and the calculated MF maps were compared with magnetization transfer ratio (MTR) and magnetization transfer saturation (MTsat) maps. Two volunteers underwent repeated multi-UTE measurements within and between days. Field-strength reproducibility and test-retest repeatability were evaluated using linear regression, Bland-Altman analysis, concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: Multi-UTE enabled simultaneous acquisition of quantitative and high-resolution structural images at both 1.5T and 3T. MF repeatability was high at 3T (ICC = 0.94-0.96) and more variable at 1.5T (0,64-0.96). Across field strengths, MF and MTsat showed comparable reproducibility (CCC 0.70 vs 0.60) with small median absolute differences (8.8% vs 8.9%). MTsat showed tighter correlation (R2 = 0.77 vs 0.68), while MF showed a wider inter-regional dynamic range. MTR differed strongly between field strengths (CCC = 0.06). Conclusion: Multi-UTE MF, obtained without B1 or T1 mapping and alongside a high-resolution structural image, achieves cross-field reproducibility comparable to, but not exceeding, MTsat. Lower SNR at 1.5T and unmodelled T1 weighting may have contributed to residual field dependence.

papers.title: A Feasibility Study of Whole-Cerebrum Task-Based fMRI at 0.55 T: Motor and Visual Tasks Using Single-Shot EPI
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the feasibility of whole-cerebrum task-based fMRI on a modern 0.55T system, examining the effects of extended scan duration and within-session consistency on functional mapping outcomes and comparison to acquisition with matched tasks at 3.0T. Methods: Six healthy participants were scanned at 0.55T using a single-shot EPI sequence during bilateral finger-tapping and visual checkerboard tasks. Data were processed using an open-source pipeline. To investigate sensitivity improvements, two consecutive 5-minute runs were concatenated. Within-session consistency was also assessed. A representative 3T dataset provided additional reference context for temporal dynamics and statistical sensitivity. Results: Task-evoked activations were detected at 0.55T using Family-Wise Error (FWE) rate correction (p < 0.05) in both motor and visual cortices. While single 5-minute runs provided baseline detectability, extending the acquisition to 10 minutes increased t-statistic magnitudes and cluster extents while substantially reducing background noise (47% reduction in voxelwise dispersion). Run-to-run comparisons showed consistent peak locations and statistical significance across participants. Comparison with the 3T reference demonstrated that statistical significance increases with acquisition time so that a 0.55T scan approximately matches 3T significance levels at twice the scan duration across the range compared. Conclusion: Whole-cerebrum task fMRI is feasible at 0.55T using standard EPI and modern high-performance gradients. These results indicate that modest extensions in scan duration can compensate for reduced intrinsic BOLD sensitivity at lower field strengths.
